Subject: Discrepancy in AWS Marketplace usage events (May 7-9)

Hi Dylan / Ben,

We're seeing a gap in recorded usage for our customers on the AWS Marketplace between May 7 03:00 UTC and May 9 22:00 UTC. Our internal billing indicates successful customer activity during that window, but the marketplace metering reports show ~18% fewer units recorded which is causing a delta in invoices.

Symptoms:
- Several customer accounts show activity in our app (events, session IDs) but no corresponding Marketplace usage records for the same timestamps.
- The gap appears intermittent and concentrated around May 8 13:45-14:05 UTC and May 9 04:00-04:20 UTC.

I've attached a small CSV snapshot with the events we have locally (usage_events_snapshot.csv) — columns: customer_id, local_timestamp, activity_type, session_id.

Can the Redwood Marketplace integration team help confirm whether events were delivered to AWS and whether any reprocessing is possible? We need to reconcile before month-end invoicing. If you need more logs from our side I can share them.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Hunter
Head of Finance & Revenue Ops
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Discrepancy in AWS Marketplace usage events (May 7-9) — diagnostics

Emma / team — quick update from instrumentation side after preliminary triage.

What we found:
- In the ingestion logs we see successful receipts of events from Acme's webhook endpoint. Those events enter our local buffer and are batched for the AWS metering submission.
- There is a repeating pattern where the local submission buffer hit backpressure for ~120 seconds due to an upstream transient (burst in requests + temporary spike in submission latency). During that window the submission worker retried and some batches were re-ordered.
- AWS metering API returned 200 for most batches, but we see ~42 requests in the timeframe that returned a 202/accepted but without an explicit usageRecordId in our response parsing. Those map to the timestamps you highlighted.

Attached: metering-diagnostics.log (excerpts) and a small subset of matched local usage records (usage_records_subset.csv).

Proposed remediation steps:
1) Create a targeted backfill file (CSV lines in AWS ingestion schema) for the affected time windows and submit to AWS reprocessing; request a fulfillment re-index for those usage units.
2) Add sequence IDs and stronger idempotency markers to submissions so we can detect / reconcile partial-acks.
3) Short-term: enable a temporary doubling of retries with exponential backoff and a tighter circuit breaker metric alert.

I can prepare the backfill CSV and a runbook for submitting to AWS — ETA for a first draft: EOD today. If AWS requires request IDs we can attempt to reconstruct from our logs.

Ben Carter
Senior Systems Engineer, Instrumentation
Redwood Inference

Hello Redwood team — this is AWS Partner Support (Case ID: 1234567890). Thanks for the diagnostic artifacts; we reviewed the submission logs and confirmed that a subset of your usage submissions were accepted but not assigned usageRecordIds due to an internal throttling and deduplication window that closed early during the spike.

Options we propose:
- We can reprocess the submitted CSV you prepare. Please format per the Marketplace SaaS Metering API CSV schema and include a unique client sequence ID per row.
- For any records without usageRecordIds, we can attempt an idempotent backfill using the 'reprocessing' flow; SLA for reprocessing is typically 3–5 business days depending on load.

Required next steps from Redwood/Acme:
1) Submit the backfill CSV link (S3 presigned or Case attachment).
2) Provide a short statement confirming the affected customer IDs and the units to be credited if reprocessing is accepted.

We have opened internal MPX ticket MPX-2245 to track the reprocess; please reference Case #1234567890 in your communications. If you'd like us to prioritize due to month-end billing, indicate urgency and provide the highest-impact customer IDs.

Regards,
